system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: This agent is instructed to follow a linear, self-iterative development process
system_prompt_style.note: Paper only; prompt mechanism not described. Per A1 paper-only rule coded static/low. Per-role prompts differ across Single/DT/DDT configs.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: it first reads the requirements document from the file system
env_context_strategy.note: Built on SWE-Agent toolset; agent reads requirements from filesystem.

context_compaction.note: Paper only; no config or history processor available. Inherits SWE-Agent foundation but pinned repo not in evidence.

observation_format.note: Observation format not described; no code in evidence.

tool_call_format.note: Parser not described; SWE-Agent foundation implies its parsers but not evidenced.

tool_count.note: Tool list not enumerated in paper.

edit_primitive.note: Edit tool not described beyond 'SWE-Agent provides a mature and flexible toolset'.

protocol_standardization.note: No dependency list or code available.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Finally, it reviews the test results and debugs the code, repeating this cycle until all tests pass.
loop_primitives.note: SWE-Agent-based react loop; test-repair cycle is prompted; DT/DDT are fixed sequential pipelines of agents. Default configuration unclear (three variants).

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: a Designer Agent, analyze the requirements document and generate a detailed project design document
planning_granularity.note: Single/DT: prompt recipe (implicit). DDT: design document handed to Developer; not clearly a stored, re-read plan object.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: We therefore simplified inter-agent collaboration, modeling it as a sequential handoff of tasks.
multi_agent_topology.note: No single default; SDAgent-Single is 'single', DT/DDT are pipelines. Best-performing DT coded.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: utilizing two agents that operate sequentially
delegation_mechanism.note: Sequential handoff; unclear whether same conversation or new agents (possibly closer to subagent_spawn). Single variant: none.

human_in_loop.note: No config surface; paper silent on human gating.

self_verification.evidence_quote: then implements the required functionality in code, creates corresponding tests, and runs these tests.
self_verification.note: Testing is prompted, not harness-enforced, so test_execution not coded; LLM judge is part of benchmark evaluation, not the agent harness.

retry_policy.note: Best-of-N discussed only as analysis (three independent runs), not a harness retry policy.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: a maximum of 200 agent steps was allocated for each task to ensure consistency and termination

cost_controls.note: Costs reported but no control mechanism described.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: an interactive sandbox environment for the agent to operate in
execution_isolation.note: Sandbox type not specified; container inferred from SWE-Agent foundation.

network_policy.note: Projects with external API calls filtered, but no network policy of harness described.

tracing.evidence_quote: we attributed failures to different stages of the agent's execution trace
tracing.note: Step-level trajectories analysed (first test writing step).

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: making our entire experimental setup publicly available for scrutiny and replication [2]
eval_hooks.note: E2EDevBench evaluation framework released with the agents; repo not inspected.

open_source.evidence_quote: A standardized, open-source implementation of end-to-end development agent system
open_source.note: Licence not verifiable; repo URL not in evidence.

model_agnostic.note: Only Gemini models used; LLM abstraction not shown (SWE-Agent uses litellm, not evidenced here).

primary_artifact.note: No repo URL provided in evidence.

first_release_date.note: Fallback: paper v1 date; no tag information.
